And the men of Israel were counted, excluding the Benjaminites: four hundred thousand men armed with swords, all of them fighting men.
The Israelites rose and went up to Bethel and inquired of God, saying, “Who will go ahead of you?”
And the Israelites rose early in the morning and went toward Gibeah.
And all the Israelites came out to fight against the Benjaminites. All the Israelites took up their positions to fight against them at Gibeah.
And the Benjaminites came out of Gibeah and killed twenty-two thousand men of Israel that day, striking them down to the ground.
And the Israelites took courage and again arranged for battle in the place where they had drawn up their ranks on the first day.

And the Israelites went up and wept before the Lord until evening. They asked the Lord, saying, “Should we continue to go and fight against the descendants of Benjamin, our brothers?” The Lord said to them, “Go against them.”
And the Israelites went against the Benjaminites on the second day.
And Benjamin came out from Gibeah to meet them on the second day. Again they struck down eighteen thousand men of Israel to the ground, all of them armed with swords.

And all the Israelites, together with all the rest of the people, got up and went up to Bethel. They wept there before the Lord and fasted that day, and they offered burnt offerings for well-being before the Lord.
And the Israelites asked the Lord, because the ark of the Lord’s covenant was there in those days.

And Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, stood before it. The Israelites asked the Lord, saying, “Should we continue to go out and fight against Benjamin, my brother, or should we stop?” The Lord said to them, “Go up against them, because tomorrow I will hand them over to you.”
And Israel set an ambush around Gibeah as a trap.
And the Israelites went up against the descendants of Benjamin on the third day, and they fought against Gibeah as they had done on the previous occasions.

And the descendants of Benjamin came out and took their stand against the people, moving away from the city. They again began striking down some of the people as before, on the roads, one of which goes up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah through the fields. They killed thirty men of Israel.

And the descendants of Benjamin said to one another, “The Israelites will fall before us again, just as they did the first time.” But the Israelites said, “Let us retreat and draw them away from the city onto the roads.”
And all the men of Israel rose up from Israel to a place and fought at Baal-tamar. And the army of Israel that was lying in ambush came out from its position in the hiding places of Gibeah.
They came out in front of Gibeah, ten thousand chosen men from all Israel. A great battle took place, but they did not know that disaster was about to come upon them.
And the Lord struck down Benjamin before Israel. That day the Israelites killed twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin, all of them armed with swords.
And Benjamin saw that they had been defeated. The men of Israel gave ground to the descendants of Benjamin because they trusted the army lying in ambush, which they had stationed near Gibeah.
And the army lying in ambush rose up and advanced against Gibeah. The army spread out, and they struck down the whole city with the edge of the sword.
And there was an agreed signal between the men of Israel and the army lying in ambush: they were to send up fire and smoke from the city as a signal.

And when the men of Israel saw that the army lying in ambush had risen and taken Gibeah, they took their stand on the battlefield. The descendants of Benjamin began killing thirty men of Israel, and they said, “Once again they are being defeated before us, just as in the first battle that took place.”
And the fire signal began rising higher above the city like a column of smoke. The descendants of Benjamin looked behind them, and there was the smoke of the city rising to the sky.
And the men of Israel turned back. The men of Benjamin, in turn, were terrified, because they saw that the evil they had done had come upon them.
And they turned away from the men of Israel toward the road leading out into the wilderness and fled there. But the army overtook them, and those in the city destroyed them in their midst.
And they struck down Benjamin, pressed them hard, and pursued them from in front of Gibeah toward the east.
And eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell, all of them capable warriors.

They turned and fled into the wilderness toward the rock of Rimmon. The Israelites pursued them and destroyed five thousand of their men. The Israelites continued pursuing them and cut them down along the roads as far as Gilead, killing two thousand of their men.
And all those of Benjamin who fell that day numbered twenty-five thousand men armed with swords, all of them strong warriors.
And the survivors turned back [?]
What shall we do about providing wives for the others who remain, who have survived? We have sworn by the Lord not to give them wives from among our daughters.
And they said, “Who among the tribes of Israel did not come up before the Lord at Mizpah?” And look, the people from Jabesh-gilead had not come up to the camp for the assembly.
The people were counted, and no one from among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead was found among them.

The assembly sent twelve thousand men from among the Israelites there, brave warriors, and commanded them, saying, “Go and strike down the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead with the edge of the sword, including the women and the people.”

“And this is what you are to do: every male and every woman who has had sexual intercourse with a man, devote them to destruction or treat them as abominations. But keep the virgins safe.” And they did these things.
They found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young virgin women who had never slept with a man. They brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.
Then the whole assembly sent word and spoke with the descendants of Benjamin at the rock of Rimmon, inviting them to be at peace with them.
At that time, the men of Benjamin returned to their brothers, the Israelites, and the Israelites gave them the women whom they had taken from among the young women [?].
